candidates.tagline: Someone bet $3M on a Spotify chart, then just… bought the chart.
candidates.story: Kalshi launched a prediction market with $3M in trading volume betting on which song would be Spotify's most-streamed in June 2026; a trader then bought over 500,000 fake streams to push obscure artist Malcolm Todd's 'Earrings' to #1, collected the payout — and Spotify only removed the fraudulent streams after the market had already been settled and winners paid, exposing the fundamental design flaw in building a financial instrument on a metric any bettor can directly manipulate.
candidates.why_funny: Kalshi spent months engineering a sophisticated prediction market on Spotify's chart data and apparently never considered that anyone with enough skin in the game could simply purchase a #1 for a fraction of the payout.
candidates.alt: A phone screen showing the Kalshi prediction market app interface displaying bet options on streaming music outcomes, photographed in Chicago, Illinois
candidates.credit: Scott Olson/Getty Images via Hollywood Reporter

candidates.tagline: 10 years of planning America's 250th birthday. They put a Ferris wheel on the Mall.
candidates.story: Congress funded America250 in 2016 to plan a once-in-a-generation dignified national celebration for the 250th anniversary; by July 4, 2026, the centerpiece of the National Mall celebrations was the first-ever 110-foot Ferris wheel installed between the Lincoln Memorial and Washington Monument, along with a rodeo, as part of Freedom 250's 'Great American State Fair' — leaving two competing organisations with competing logos both claiming to run the country's birthday party.
candidates.why_funny: Ten years and a Congressional appropriation to plan the most significant national birthday since the founding, and the landmark addition to the country's most sacred civic lawn was a carnival ride.
candidates.alt: An ornate decorative arch in the foreground with a large 110-foot Ferris wheel dominating the mid-ground and the Washington Monument visible in the background on the National Mall, Washington DC, June 26, 2026
